property_summary: For all initialize inputs, the reference contract records baseToken equal to the _baseToken parameter passed to initialize; the mutant that forces baseToken = address(0) violates this when _baseToken != address(0).

For any initialize(...) call, the contract's public baseToken getter returns the _baseToken argument passed to initialize; the mutant breaks this by setting baseToken = _nft so baseToken != _baseToken for some inputs.

For any caller and any _baseToken argument, after initialize(...) completes the reference contract sets baseToken to the passed _baseToken; the mutant instead sets baseToken = msg.sender and thus can make baseToken != _baseToken for some inputs.

For any input parameters, the reference contract allows initialize(...) to succeed regardless of whether _baseToken is address(0) (i.e. initialization does not reject a zero base token), whereas the mutant rejects (reverts) whenever _baseToken == address(0).

For every input parameters to initialize(...), the reference contract always allows initialization to succeed (does not revert) when called on a fresh instance, including when _baseToken == address(0); the mutant introduces a require that reverts when _baseToken == address(0), so there exist fuzzed inputs (with _baseToken == address(0)) for which the mutant rejects while the reference accepts.
